claude.rationale: This was a whole-entity cash merger in which "legal vehicle, subsidiaries, and customer-facing wire/cable product business all crossed together," so the customer-facing product (T4) and the operations/subsidiaries producing it (T5) transferred coherently as a single going concern — no product-vs-process mismatch, hence gap_45=0. The same whole-entity transfer carried operations together with continuing employees (base pay/benefits preserved through the first anniversary) and retained two prior administrative officers, so processes and organization moved together despite the board/NEO replacement — hence gap_56=0. T6 is coded partial because the entire board and named-executive slate ceased serving while the broader workforce continued, and T1 is replace since Prysmian installed new controlling intent (new CEO Battaini) over the surviving subsidiary.

gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-entity merger where the legal vehicle, subsidiaries, and customer-facing wire/cable product business all crossed together at closing. Because the entire operating entity transferred intact, there is no documented structural mismatch between products and processes (gap_45 = 0) or processes and the organization (gap_56 = 0).

grok.rationale: The structural summary and 8-K Items 5.01/5.02 state that the surviving General Cable entity, subsidiaries, and customer-facing wire/cable product business all crossed together into Prysmian ownership at the June 6, 2018 effective time, so T4 product and T5 processes moved as one bundle with no product-vs-process mismatch at closing (gap_45=0). Continuing-employee base pay, benefits, bonus, and severance commitments in the DEFM14A kept the operating workforce aligned with those processes at closing, while only the board and named-executive slate were replaced; that leadership swap does not constitute processes transferring without the organization substrate (gap_56=0).
